en: I am perpetually prostrate before Rāmacandra, who is beyond all calculation of qualities, immeasurable, the primordial source, the cause of the maintenance and dissolution of the entire universe, the supreme state of cessation, and the very self of the Supreme Being. || 1 ||

I perpetually bow to Rāma, the best of men, the granter of boons, who holds an excellent bow and arrows in his hands; he possesses the side-long glances of Lakṣmī, which grant boundless happiness and destroy the sufferings of Indra, Brahmā, and others.

I take refuge in the joy of the Raghus, whose form is beloved by the three worlds, who is worthy of praise, as radiant as a hundred suns, the bestower of desired boons, the eternal giver of shelter, and who has made his abode at the foot of the celestial tree. || 3 ||

I take refuge in Hari, who is named the forest fire for the jungle of worldly existence, who is the deity presiding over the deities of the mouth of worldly existence, who is compassionate, who is the destroyer of thousands of crores of lords of the Danujas, and who is like the son of the Sun (Yama). || 4 ||

Ever visible to the sages who have renounced worldly existence and are far removed from the contemplation of saṃsāra, I take refuge in the Joy of the Raghus, the boat-like feet for crossing the ocean of existence. || 5 ||

I take refuge in the Lord of the Raghus, the bestower of boons upon the gods, whose feet are served by the foremost of deities and the lords of the asuras; he who dwells in the hearts of Śiva and Pārvatī, who bears the king of mountains, and who is delightful through his divine deeds. || 6 ||

I take refuge in the lotus-eyed, best of the Raghus, who is easily accessible to those who refrain from the wealth and wives of others, whose minds are satisfied by the virtues and prosperity of others, and whose very selves are devoted to the welfare of others. 7.

I take refuge in the Lord of the Raghus, the preceptor of the preceptor of the gods; whose lotus-face is blossomed with the radiance of a smile, who is most easily accessible, who is as dark as the sapphire of the king of the gods, and whose beauty is graced by eyes like lovely white lotuses.

Through the distinctions of the forms of Hari, Kamalaja, and Śambhu, you shine here, following the three qualities (guṇas), like the sun in water-filled vessels; I praise the Lord, the worthy object of praise for the King of the Immortals.

I take refuge in the Lord, the Master of the Raghus, who removes all suffering; whose body is more beautiful than hundreds of millions of Cupids, who is far beyond the reach of meditation on the path of the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, and who shines eternally within the heart of the Lord of Ascetics. 10.
As he was thus praising him, the best of the Raghus became pleased and said:
"Go, may prosperity be yours; [this is] my supreme station, Viṣṇu's."
Whoever hears this hymn, or writes it down, or recites it with self-restraint,
shall attain a form similar to mine and obtain mindfulness of me at the time of death.
Having heard these words spoken by Rāghava at that time, the twice-born man was overwhelmed with joy.
Having attained equality with Raghunandana, he departed for that state which is highly honored by Brahmā.
Thus ends the hymn to Śrī Rāma composed by Jaṭāyu in the eighth canto of the Araṇyakāṇḍa of the glorious Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa.
